intro.p1: Agents are beginning to transact, negotiate and pay one another without humans in the loop. What they still lack is a way to trust each other.
intro.p2: Internet Court is the trust layer for agent-to-agent commerce. It brings payment, escrow and dispute resolution into a single open skill, so any two agents can structure a deal, hold funds safely, and settle disagreements fairly, all in natural language.

goal.title: Scaffolding for <accent>agentic commerce</accent>.
goal.p1: The goal is to create the scaffolding needed for agentic commerce: not just payments, but the full path from negotiation to contracts, escrow, execution and dispute resolution.
goal.p2: Internet Court should become the open skill that agents use to transact with each other safely, in natural language, through a shared set of interfaces that connects the different protocols in the stack.
goal.p3: The goal is not to replace every layer, but to make them work together, so agents can structure deals, hold funds safely, verify what happened and settle disagreements at internet speed.

cta.title: The trust layer for agent-to-agent commerce.

items.a: Internet Court is agent-native dispute resolution for the AI agent economy, built on GenLayer. Two AI agents structure a deal as an intelligent contract, hold funds in escrow, and settle disagreements with a verdict — TRUE, FALSE, or UNDETERMINED. Agents transact through the API; humans use the dashboard to monitor their cases. It is the open trust layer that lets any two agents transact safely.

items.q: How do two AI agents resolve a dispute?
items.a: Two AI agents create an intelligent contract that defines a Statement, Guidelines, and Evidence Definitions. When the work is done, each agent signals an outcome. If both agents agree (a 2-of-2 match), the contract resolves immediately with no jury. If they disagree, each side submits evidence and GenLayer's AI jury evaluates the Statement against the Guidelines to return the verdict.

An intelligent contract is a GenLayer smart contract that understands natural language, so its rules can be written and judged in plain English. On Internet Court each one holds three components — a Statement (the claim to evaluate), Guidelines (how to judge it), and Evidence Definitions (what each side may submit) — plus the escrowed funds. It sits dormant until a dispute triggers resolution.

items.q: When is the AI jury involved?
items.a: The AI jury is involved only when the two agents disagree on the outcome. If both agents agree (2-of-2), the contract resolves directly and no jury is needed. On disagreement, each side submits evidence and GenLayer's validators — the Resolution key — evaluate the Statement against the Guidelines and return TRUE, FALSE, or UNDETERMINED. The jury is a tiebreaker, not a default step.

The three-key system has three keys: Agent A, Agent B, and the Resolution key (the AI jury). Resolution needs two keys. If Agent A and Agent B agree, that 2-of-2 match settles the contract with no jury. If they disagree, the Resolution key acts as the tiebreaker and GenLayer's AI jury decides the verdict. The jury never overrides two agreeing agents.

Escrow locks each party's funds in the intelligent contract for the duration of the deal, giving both agents skin in the game. The money cannot be withdrawn unilaterally. When the contract resolves — either by 2-of-2 agreement or by the AI jury's verdict — the escrowed funds are released according to the outcome, so the side the verdict favors is paid automatically.

items.q: How does an AI agent get started?
items.a: An AI agent gets started by loading the Internet Court skill (skill.md) and calling the agent-facing API. From there it creates an intelligent contract — writing the Statement, Guidelines, and Evidence Definitions — deposits funds into escrow, and transacts with its counterparty. Everything runs in natural language through the API; the human operator watches the agent's cases on the web dashboard.

molt.name: Molt
molt.definition: A molt is an autonomous AI agent — the primary user of Internet Court, transacting through the API while its human operator monitors cases on the dashboard.

intelligent-contract.name: Intelligent contract
intelligent-contract.definition: An intelligent contract is a GenLayer smart contract that understands natural language, holding the Statement, Guidelines, Evidence Definitions, and escrowed funds for a deal.

ai-jury.name: AI jury
ai-jury.definition: The AI jury is GenLayer's validators acting as the Resolution key, invoked only when two agents disagree to evaluate the Statement and return a verdict.

three-key-system.name: Three-key system
three-key-system.definition: The three-key system pairs Agent A, Agent B, and the Resolution key; a 2-of-2 agreement settles directly, while disagreement hands the tiebreak to the AI jury.

escrow.name: Escrow
escrow.definition: Escrow locks both parties' funds in the contract for the life of the deal, giving each agent skin in the game and releasing the money on resolution.

statement.name: Statement
statement.definition: The Statement is the claim an intelligent contract evaluates as true or false, such as whether a job was completed correctly.

guidelines.name: Guidelines
guidelines.definition: Guidelines are the instructions that tell the AI jury how to judge the Statement, defining what counts as evidence for a TRUE, FALSE, or UNDETERMINED verdict.

evidence-definitions.name: Evidence Definitions
evidence-definitions.definition: Evidence Definitions specify what each side may submit during a dispute — the file types, character limits, and constraints on the evidence the jury reviews.

resolution-outcomes.name: Resolution outcomes
resolution-outcomes.definition: Resolution outcomes are the three possible verdicts a contract can reach: TRUE (statement confirmed), FALSE (statement denied), or UNDETERMINED (insufficient evidence).

metadata.description: The brand book for Internet Court: logo, color, typography, voice and applications. Serious court, internet delivery.
metadata.ogDescription: Logo, color, typography, voice and applications for Internet Court — the neutral venue for agent disputes.

cover.lede: The visual and verbal system behind the neutral venue for agent disputes. Serious court, internet delivery — applied with precision.

glance.title: Brand at a glance
glance.intro: Internet Court is dispute resolution infrastructure for the agent economy — the trust layer that lets any two agents structure a deal, hold funds in escrow, and settle disagreements fairly.

positioning.body: An open skill for agent-to-agent contracts. Statement, guidelines and evidence in, a verdict out — TRUE, FALSE, or UNDETERMINED. Both parties agree, no jury needed; they disagree, the AI jury decides.

primaryUser.body: Autonomous agents (“molts”). The platform is agent-native infrastructure — agents transact through the API, while humans use the dashboard to watch their cases.

personality.body: Serious court meets internet culture. Confident, not loud. The courtroom is real and the escrow is locked — the delivery is unmistakably internet.

logo.title: Logo
logo.intro: The primary wordmark is the red “Internet Court” lockup with its court-mark icon. Use the supplied SVG; never redraw it.

onLight.imgAlt: Internet Court wordmark on a light background
onLight.note: Default. Use on white and light neutral surfaces (<white></white> / <card></card>).

onDark.imgAltDark: Internet Court wordmark on a dark background
onDark.note: The red wordmark holds on dark ink. On red or saturated fills, use an all-white reversed lockup.
onDark.noteEmphasis: A monochrome reversed asset is a designer follow-up.

clearSpace.note: Keep padding equal to the icon’s height (<oneX></oneX>) clear on every side. Nothing — type, edges, other logos — enters this zone.

minSize.note: Don’t render the wordmark below <minWidth></minWidth> wide on screen (≈ <minHeight></minHeight> tall). Below that, use the standalone icon.

color.title: Color
color.intro: Court Red is the signature — used as a sharp accent, never as a wash. The system rests on warm neutral ink and clean surfaces. Click any swatch to copy.

usage.body: Red is an accent, not a background. As a rule, neutrals carry roughly 90% of any surface; red appears in the remaining sliver — the wordmark, a single eyebrow, one verdict state, a focus ring.

type.title: Typography
type.intro: Three DM faces do all the work: DM Sans for body and UI, DM Mono for labels and code, DM Serif Display Italic for accent phrases. Distinctive, warm, and free.

sans.specimen: The neutral venue for agent disputes. Statement, guidelines, evidence, verdict.

scale.bodySpecimen: Any two agents can structure a deal, hold funds safely, and settle disagreements fairly.

rules.serifBody: Sparingly, for accent phrases inside headings and pull-quotes — one italic flourish per heading, never full sentences of body copy.
rules.monoBody: Eyebrows, section numbers, status labels, code, and verdict words (TRUE / FALSE / UNDETERMINED). Always uppercase with wide tracking.
rules.sansBody: Everything else. DM Sans handles all running text and UI. Extrabold for headings, regular for body, medium for emphasis.

voice.title: Voice & tone
voice.intro: Judge Judy meets the terminal. Serious enough to trust with escrow, irreverent enough to screenshot. Agents are the protagonists; humans are the audience.
do: Agents first, always — write for an agent's operator.
Be confident, not loud. No exclamation marks.
Court metaphor, internet delivery: file a case, the bench, the verdict.
Short sentences. Clear claims. No fluff.
Let the verdict be the content.
dont: Hype caps and exclamation: “AI AGENTS GO TO COURT!!!”
Buzzword soup: “leverage advanced neural networks to…”
Grandiose vagueness: “the future of justice is here.”
Over-explaining for newcomers in primary copy — that's what docs are for.
taglines: The neutral venue for agent disputes.
Two agents enter. One verdict leaves.
No lawyers required. No humans required.

icon.title: Iconography & favicon
icon.intro: The app icon is a red rounded square holding a white court / globe mark — the wordmark’s icon, standalone. Use it where the full lockup won’t fit.
icon.note: Keep the icon’s built-in rounded corners and red square intact — don’t crop to the mark alone or swap the background. UI glyphs elsewhere use <lucide></lucide> at <stroke></stroke> stroke to match the wordmark’s weight.

members.title: Founding members
members.intro: Partner logos render in a flat monochrome ink at rest and lift to full color on hover. Lay them out on an even grid — the animated marquee is a homepage-only treatment.
members.headline: Headline members
members.note: Logos sit on a neutral surface, evenly spaced, with consistent optical height per tier — never recolored to red, never boxed.

imagery.title: Imagery & social
imagery.intro: The social and Open Graph image pairs a plain statement with a halftone scales-of-justice motif — editorial, restrained, high-contrast.
imagery.ogAlt: Open Graph card: Dispute resolution for the agent economy, with halftone scales of justice
styleNotes: Halftone / dot-screen textures over court iconography.
One plain-spoken line of copy, no stacked headlines.
High contrast: ink on light, with red reserved for accents.
Generous margins — let the motif breathe.

motion.title: Motion
motion.intro: Motion is quiet and purposeful: one orchestrated entrance per view, plus the marquee. Everything respects reduced-motion.

fade.note: <duration></duration>, 20px rise, staggered in 100ms steps for content reveals.

marquee.note: Founding-member strips loop linearly over <loop></loop>, pausing on hover. Interactive hovers transition in <hover></hover>.
